All findings below were reconstructed from that session's terse notes file (review_log/findings/phase1_base-pipeline.md) plus its transcript extract, then independently re-verified in the current tree: the collect_stats/train shared-config mutation, the TEMPLATE demo.yaml exp_tag crash, the pack_demo/upload_demo log+pip-freeze leak, the config_utils import-time basicConfig issue, the _has_exp_identity docstring/interpolation bug, and the --dry_run mkdir side effect were all re-run live in this session (fresh scratch scripts under SCRATCH/base-pipeline) and reproduced exactly; the README/metrics.yaml missing-inference_dir bug and the create_dataset func/dataset_dir dead-kwargs issue were re-derived by reading current source/config lines plus targeted greps (no consumer of the `func` key was found anywhere). The original session's already-executed 'demo bundle contents' script (pack_demo/upload_demo log+pip-freeze leaking into the shipped bundle) was recovered directly from the raw tool_result in the session's transcript jsonl, which contains the actual command output confirming the leak, so no re-execution was needed for that one. assumptions: 'Default recipe path' for stage-mutation bugs (finding 1) is read as: `python run.py --training_config ...` with no explicit `--stages` flag, which is the tool's own argparse default (all DEFAULT_STAGES in one process) -- not the split-invocation style shown in the librispeech README steps.

Multi-GPU/DDP behavior (finding 9) is inferred from reading espnet3/components/trainers/trainer.py, stages_utils.py and lightning's subprocess_script.py launcher source (as the original session did) rather than from an actual multi-rank run.

findings.summary: collect_stats() destructively pops model.normalize/model.normalize_conf out of the shared training_config DictConfig, so a train() call in the same process silently builds the model without the configured normalization layer.
findings.scenario: Run `python run.py --training_config conf/tuning/training_e_branchformer.yaml` with no --stages flag (argparse default expands to all DEFAULT_STAGES, i.e. create_dataset, train_tokenizer, collect_stats, train, ... in one process against the SAME BaseSystem.training_config object). The real librispeech_100 recipe config sets `model.normalize: global_mvn` with `normalize_conf.stats_file`. collect_stats() pops both keys from config.model in place (config.model is the exact DictConfig node also referenced by self.training_config, reused for the train() call that follows in the same run). The subsequent train() therefore instantiates the ASR model without a `normalize`/`normalize_conf` key at all, so the model falls back to ESPnet2's default normalization (UtteranceMVN) instead of the global_mvn statistics the user configured and just computed -- silently wrong training, not a crash.
findings.evidence: training.py:62-65: `if "normalize" in config.model: config.model.pop("normalize")` / `if "normalize_conf" in config.model: config.model.pop("normalize_conf")`. Called via system.py:294 `return collect_stats(self.training_config)` and system.py:309 `return train(self.training_config)` -- same `self.training_config` object both times. egs3/librispeech_100/asr/conf/tuning/training_e_branchformer.yaml:112-113 sets `normalize: global_mvn` / `normalize_conf: ...`. Verified end-to-end in this session: a config with `normalize: global_mvn` run through `training.collect_stats(cfg)` then `get_espnet_model(cfg.task, cfg.model)` (what train() would build) produced `type(m.normalize).__name__ == "UtteranceMVN"`, not GlobalMVN.
findings.suggested_fix: Operate on a copy of config (or config.model) inside collect_stats() -- e.g. `local_cfg = OmegaConf.create(OmegaConf.to_container(config))` before popping -- so the caller's training_config is never mutated as a side effect of collect_stats().

findings.summary: The exact 'Common usage' command documented for the measure stage (README and metrics.yaml's own header comment) crashes with a raw ConfigAttributeError because inference_dir is only propagated into metrics_config from inference_config, never from training_config.
findings.scenario: Follow egs3/librispeech_100/asr/readme.md step 3 verbatim: `python run.py --stages measure --training_config conf/tuning/training_e_branchformer.yaml --metrics_config conf/metrics.yaml` (no --inference_config). metrics.yaml itself declares no `dataset.test` and no `inference_dir` (only comments describing it). `apply_training_experiment_context` only copies exp_tag/exp_dir (not inference_dir) from training_config into metrics_config (run_utils.py _TRAINING_CONTEXT_KEYS), and only copies inference_dir from inference_config into metrics_config when inference_config is also given (run_utils.py:389-397). Since inference_config is None here, metrics_config.inference_dir is never set. measure() -> _resolve_test_sets() then evaluates `Path(metrics_config.inference_dir)` via plain attribute access, raising `omegaconf.errors.ConfigAttributeError: Missing key inference_dir` instead of a clear user-facing error.
findings.evidence: espnet3/systems/base/metric.py:24 `inference_dir = Path(metrics_config.inference_dir)` (no .get()/default). espnet3/utils/run_utils.py:389-397 gates the inference_dir copy on `inference_config is not None and metrics_config is not None`. egs3/librispeech_100/asr/readme.md:20-22 and egs3/librispeech_100/asr/conf/metrics.yaml:4-6 both document exactly the failing invocation (--training_config + --metrics_config, no --inference_config).
findings.suggested_fix: Either also copy inference_dir from training_config.exp_dir-derived defaults when no inference_config is supplied, or have _resolve_test_sets raise the same clear ValueError used elsewhere ('measure stage requires ... inference_dir') via metrics_config.get('inference_dir') instead of attribute access; alternatively fix the docs to always pass --inference_config alongside --metrics_config.

findings.summary: The documented 'Quick usage' for pack_demo/upload_demo (--demo_config only, no --training_config) crashes with InterpolationKeyError('exp_tag') because demo.yaml's default model.dir_or_tag references ${exp_tag}, which is only ever populated from training_config.
findings.scenario: Run `python run.py --stages pack_demo --demo_config conf/demo.yaml` exactly as documented in TEMPLATE/asr/conf/demo.yaml's own header (and inherited by mini_an4/librispeech_100, whose run.py both call the same `main()` imported from egs3.TEMPLATE.asr.run, so `load_and_merge_config(..., default_package=__package__, ...)` always merges TEMPLATE's demo.yaml -- including its `model.dir_or_tag: exp/${exp_tag}/model_pack` default -- underneath every recipe's own demo.yaml). Because --training_config is omitted, `load_and_merge_config` returns training_config=None (config_utils.py:395-396), so `apply_training_experiment_context`'s `if training_config is not None:` guard (run_utils.py:351) skips copying exp_tag into demo_config entirely. `resolve_loaded_configs(..., demo_config)` (run.py) then calls `OmegaConf.resolve(demo_config)`, which raises `InterpolationKeyError: Interpolation key 'exp_tag' not found` before pack_demo's own clear `ValueError('demo_config.model.dir_or_tag is required...')` check (packing.py:334-336) is ever reached.
findings.evidence: egs3/TEMPLATE/asr/conf/demo.yaml:4-5 'Quick usage: python run.py --stages pack_demo --demo_config conf/demo.yaml'; line 24 `dir_or_tag: exp/${exp_tag}/model_pack`. espnet3/utils/config_utils.py:395-396 `if config_path is None: return None`. espnet3/utils/run_utils.py:351,379-387 (exp_tag only copied when training_config is not None). egs3/mini_an4/asr/run.py:1-6 and egs3/librispeech_100/asr/run.py:1-6 both `from egs3.TEMPLATE.asr.run import ... main` and call it unmodified, so `__package__` inside main() is always `egs3.TEMPLATE.asr`, meaning every recipe's demo_config default-merges against TEMPLATE's demo.yaml. Reproduced live in this session: `_has_exp_identity`/interpolation resolution against `OmegaConf.create({"exp_dir": "${exp_tag}/foo"})` raises `InterpolationKeyError: Interpolation key 'exp_tag' not found` when exp_tag is not a key in the config at all (the exact shape produced by the Quick-usage path).
findings.suggested_fix: Either declare a placeholder `exp_tag: null` (or similar) with an explicit fallback in demo.yaml so resolution doesn't hard-fail, or have run.py validate demo-stage experiment identity the same way validate_experiment_context() does for infer/measure before calling resolve_loaded_configs, so users get the clear 'demo requires --training_config or exp_tag' message instead of a raw OmegaConf traceback.

findings.summary: set_stage_log_handler(None, ...) returns early without removing the previous stage's file handler, so on non-zero ranks in rank0 stage_log_mode the prior stage's log file keeps silently absorbing every later stage's log records for the rest of the process.
findings.scenario: In stages_utils.py's run_stages(), the "train" stage sets `log_dir = None` for any rank != 0 when stage_log_mode is the default "rank0" (stages_utils.py:165-167), then calls `set_stage_log_handler(None, filename=...)`. set_stage_log_handler's very first check is `if log_dir is None: return None` (logging_utils.py:270-271) -- this exits before the handler-removal loop a few lines below (lines 274-277) ever runs. So on a non-zero-rank worker, whatever `_espnet3_stage_log` FileHandler was installed by the previous stage (e.g. collect_stats, which runs in the same process ahead of train and is not rank-gated) stays attached to the root logger and keeps receiving every subsequent log record -- including the entire train stage's output -- for the rest of the run, and its file handle is never closed.
findings.evidence: logging_utils.py:257-271 `def set_stage_log_handler(log_dir, filename): ... if log_dir is None: return None` -- occurs before the `for handler in list(root.handlers): if getattr(handler, "_espnet3_stage_log", False): root.removeHandler(handler); handler.close()` cleanup at lines 274-277. stages_utils.py:165-167 `if stage_log_mode == "rank0" and rank != 0: log_dir = None`.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the stale-handler removal loop above the `if log_dir is None: return None` early return (or extract it into its own always-run step) so a None log_dir still detaches any previously-installed stage handler.

findings.summary: run_stages() blanket-catches TypeError from inside a stage's implementation and always re-raises it as a misleading "Stage does not accept CLI arguments" error, even when the TypeError has nothing to do with CLI arguments.
findings.scenario: Stage methods on BaseSystem reject *args/**kwargs up front via _reject_stage_args before doing any real work (system.py:191-198), so by the time `fn()` executes inside run_stages' try block, any TypeError that still occurs is necessarily from deep inside the stage's own logic (a bad Hydra `instantiate()` target signature, a misconfigured metric class, a bug in a user's dataset builder, etc.), not from CLI argument handling. run_stages nonetheless catches every TypeError and re-raises it as `TypeError(f"Stage '{stage}' does not accept CLI arguments; put all settings in the YAML config.") from e`, discarding the real error's message from the user-visible exception type/text (the original is preserved only as `__cause__`) and actively pointing the user at the wrong root cause.
findings.evidence: stages_utils.py:183-190: `try: fn() except TypeError as e: log.exception(...); raise TypeError(f"Stage '{stage}' does not accept CLI arguments; put all settings in the YAML config.") from e`. Contrast with system.py:192-198's `_reject_stage_args`, which is the only place a real 'stage does not accept arguments' TypeError should originate, and which already fires before `fn()` is even entered from the caller's perspective (fn() is always called with zero args: `fn()` at stages_utils.py:184).
findings.suggested_fix: Only apply the CLI-arguments framing to a TypeError raised by _reject_stage_args itself (e.g. tag it with a distinguishing attribute, or just let it propagate straight from BaseSystem's own **kwargs check rather than a generic runner-level `except TypeError`), and let any other TypeError from within a stage propagate with its original message.

findings.summary: pack_demo and upload_demo stage logs are written directly into demo_config.pack.out_dir -- the same directory upload_demo then ships wholesale to the Hugging Face Space -- and --write_requirements makes upload_demo overwrite the user's curated pack.requirements list with a full local `pip freeze` dump before shipping it.
findings.scenario: Run `python run.py --stages pack_demo upload_demo --demo_config conf/demo.yaml --write_requirements`. BaseSystem's stage_log_dirs mapping points both "pack_demo" and "upload_demo" at `demo_config.pack.out_dir` (system.py:139-140), which is exactly the directory pack_demo() populates and upload_demo() later uploads with `api.upload_folder(..., folder_path=str(demo_dir), ...)` (packing.py). run_stages() installs each stage's file log there via set_stage_log_handler, and log_run_metadata's --write_requirements path calls `_write_requirements_snapshot`, which locates the *current* log file's directory (i.e. the demo bundle dir) and writes `requirements.txt` there from a full `pip freeze`/`uv pip freeze` -- clobbering the curated requirements.txt that pack_demo's own `_write_requirements()` (packing.py:193) had already written from `demo_config.pack.requirements`. Reproduced live in the original review session (recovered from that session's transcript): after running pack_demo then upload_demo with write_requirements=True, the bundle directory upload_folder ships contained `['app.py', 'pack_demo.log', 'requirements.txt', 'upload_demo.log']`, and requirements.txt's first lines were a full pip-freeze dump (`absl-py==2.5.0, aiohappyeyeballs==2.7.1, aiohttp==3.14.3, ...`) instead of the curated `['espnet', 'gradio']` list configured in pack.requirements.
findings.evidence: system.py:139-140 `"pack_demo": "demo_config.pack.out_dir", "upload_demo": "demo_config.pack.out_dir"`. packing.py upload_demo() uploads `folder_path=str(demo_dir)` where demo_dir == the same out_dir. logging_utils.py:396-417 `_write_requirements_snapshot` resolves the log directory from the active FileHandler and writes `requirements.txt` there unconditionally when write_requirements is set (logging_utils.py ~521-522 in log_run_metadata). Live verification output (this session, read from the earlier session's raw tool_result): `upload_folder would ship: ['app.py', 'pack_demo.log', 'requirements.txt', 'upload_demo.log']` and `requirements.txt first lines: ['absl-py==2.5.0', 'aiohappyeyeballs==2.7.1', 'aiohttp==3.14.3']` after running pack_demo+upload_demo with write_requirements=True against a curated pack.requirements=['espnet','gradio'].
findings.suggested_fix: Write stage logs (and any --write_requirements snapshot) to a location outside the packaged demo directory -- e.g. under system.exp_dir/logs -- rather than reusing demo_config.pack.out_dir as the stage log dir; or have pack_demo explicitly re-assert/protect its curated requirements.txt after log setup, and have upload_demo's folder_path exclude *.log/requirements.txt written by the logging layer.

findings.summary: config_utils registers its OmegaConf resolvers at import time using module-level logging.info(), which implicitly triggers logging.basicConfig() and installs a bare-format StreamHandler before configure_logging() ever runs -- so configure_logging()'s own formatted console handler is silently skipped and every console log line loses hostname/stage/timestamp formatting.
findings.scenario: Any process that imports espnet3.utils.config_utils before calling configure_logging() (which is every run.py entrypoint, since config loading happens before `logger = configure_logging()`) triggers, at import time, `logging.info(f"Registered ESPnet-3 OmegaConf Resolver: {name}")` for each of 4 resolvers. Because these are the bare `logging.info()` module-level convenience calls (not calls on a named logger) and the root logger has no handlers yet, Python's logging module auto-invokes `logging.basicConfig()`, attaching a default `StreamHandler` with format `%(levelname)s:%(name)s:%(message)s` to the root logger. When configure_logging() later runs, its guard `if not any(isinstance(h, logging.StreamHandler) for h in root.handlers)` sees that basicConfig's StreamHandler already satisfies `isinstance(h, logging.StreamHandler)` and skips installing its own handler with LOG_FORMAT (hostname/timestamp/stage). Console output for the rest of the run uses the bare basicConfig format, not the documented LOG_FORMAT.
findings.evidence: config_utils.py:151-156: `for name, resolver in OMEGACONF_ESPNET3_RESOLVER.items(): OmegaConf.register_new_resolver(name, resolver); logging.info(f"Registered ESPnet-3 OmegaConf Resolver: {name}")` at module scope. logging_utils.py:226-229 `if not any(isinstance(h, logging.StreamHandler) for h in root.handlers): stream = logging.StreamHandler(); ...; root.addHandler(stream)`. Verified live in this session: `root handlers before import: []` -> `root handlers after config_utils import: [<StreamHandler <stderr> (NOTSET)>]` -> after calling configure_logging(log_dir=None), the single remaining handler's formatter `_fmt` is still `'%(levelname)s:%(name)s:%(message)s'`, not LOG_FORMAT.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a module logger (`logging.getLogger(__name__).info(...)`) instead of the bare `logging.info(...)` convenience call for the resolver-registration messages, so importing config_utils never has the side effect of calling logging.basicConfig() on the root logger.

findings.summary: _has_exp_identity's own docstring example claims it returns False for an exp_dir containing an unresolved ${exp_tag}, but it actually raises InterpolationKeyError, and that exception propagates straight out of validate_experiment_context, replacing its intended clear ValueError with a confusing OmegaConf traceback.
findings.scenario: Call `_has_exp_identity(OmegaConf.create({"exp_dir": "${exp_tag}/foo"}))` -- exactly the docstring's own example at run_utils.py:73, which claims the call 'returns False'. In fact `config.get("exp_dir")` at line 79 resolves the interpolation by default; since exp_tag is not a key anywhere in this config, OmegaConf raises `InterpolationKeyError: Interpolation key 'exp_tag' not found` instead of returning False. Because validate_experiment_context() calls _has_exp_identity() directly inside its own try-less body (run_utils.py:510,517) to decide whether to raise its clear 'infer/measure stage requires --training_config or ... exp_tag/exp_dir' ValueError, any standalone inference_config/metrics_config whose exp_dir template still contains ${exp_tag} (and that never declares an exp_tag key at all, e.g. a hand-authored config copied without the exp_tag: placeholder) crashes with the raw InterpolationKeyError instead of the intended guidance message.
findings.evidence: run_utils.py:71-73 docstring: '`OmegaConf.create({"exp_dir": "${exp_tag}/foo"})` returns `False`.' vs. implementation at line 79 `exp_dir = config.get("exp_dir")` (resolves interpolations by default) and line 82 `return "${exp_tag}" not in exp_dir ...` (dead code once line 79 has already raised). Verified live in this session: `_has_exp_identity(OmegaConf.create({"exp_dir": "${exp_tag}/foo"}))` raises `InterpolationKeyError: Interpolation key 'exp_tag' not found`, and `validate_experiment_context(training_config=None, inference_config=that_cfg, metrics_config=None, stages_to_run=["infer"])` raises the same InterpolationKeyError rather than its documented ValueError. Note: the crash requires the exp_tag key to be entirely absent, not merely None -- egs3/TEMPLATE and egs3/librispeech_100's inference.yaml/metrics.yaml both declare `exp_tag:` (present, value None), which returns False cleanly; the crash is reachable via a hand-authored standalone config that omits the exp_tag key, or via the docstring's own literal example.
findings.suggested_fix: Call `config.get("exp_dir", None)` with an explicit `OmegaConf` resolve=False, or wrap the interpolation check in a try/except InterpolationResolutionError returning False, so an undefined exp_tag inside exp_dir is treated the same as a missing exp_tag rather than raising.

findings.summary: BaseSystem.__init__ unconditionally creates exp_dir on disk before --dry_run is ever consulted, so `run.py --dry_run` still has a real filesystem side effect despite its help text promising to only print what would run.
findings.scenario: `main()` in egs3/TEMPLATE/asr/run.py constructs `system = system_cls(training_config=training_config, ...)` (which runs BaseSystem.__init__) before calling run_stages(system, stages_to_run, args, log) at the very end of main(). --dry_run is only checked inside run_stages's per-stage loop (stages_utils.py:137,144-146), by which point BaseSystem.__init__ has already executed `self.exp_dir = Path(training_config.exp_dir); self.exp_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` unconditionally. Running `python run.py --training_config conf/training.yaml --dry_run` therefore still creates the experiment directory on disk, contradicting the flag's documented behavior ('Print what would be executed without actually running stages.').
findings.evidence: system.py:120-122: `if training_config is not None: self.exp_dir = Path(training_config.exp_dir); self.exp_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` -- runs inside `__init__`, unconditional on dry_run. stages_utils.py:137,144-146 -- dry_run is only read inside run_stages, called after system construction in run.py's main(). Verified live in this session: constructing `BaseSystem(training_config=OmegaConf.create({"exp_dir": "dryrun_exp"}))` alone (no run_stages call at all) creates `dryrun_exp/` on disk.
findings.suggested_fix: Defer the exp_dir mkdir until the first stage that actually needs it runs (or gate it on a `dry_run` flag passed into BaseSystem), rather than doing it as a side effect of construction.

findings.summary: create_dataset() forwards the entire training_config.create_dataset block (including a `func` key that looks like a factory-function reference) as **kwargs to every DatasetBuilder method, but no code anywhere ever reads or calls `func` -- it is silently absorbed by builders' `**_kwargs` catch-alls, so a stale/wrong `func` value gives no signal that it is dead.
findings.scenario: egs3/TEMPLATE/asr/conf/training.yaml declares `create_dataset: {func: src.creating_dataset.create_dataset, dataset_dir: ${dataset_dir}}` -- naming strongly suggesting `func` is a dotted path to a callable that create_dataset() will invoke (matching the general Hydra-ish `_target_`/`func`-as-factory convention used elsewhere in this codebase). In fact, BaseSystem.create_dataset() only ever calls the fixed methods `builder.is_source_prepared(**builder_kwargs)`, `builder.prepare_source(**builder_kwargs)`, `builder.is_built(**builder_kwargs)`, `builder.build(**builder_kwargs)` where `builder_kwargs` is a plain `dict(create_dataset_config)` copy that still contains `func`; real recipe builders (e.g. egs3/mini_an4/asr/dataset/builder.py) declare these methods as `def is_source_prepared(self, recipe_dir, **_kwargs)`, so `func` is silently swallowed by `**_kwargs` on every call, never imported or invoked anywhere in the codebase. A user who renames/deletes `src/creating_dataset.py`'s create_dataset function gets zero feedback that the reference is now stale, and a user reading the config would reasonably but incorrectly assume changing `func` changes dataset-creation behavior.
findings.evidence: system.py:236-239 `create_dataset_config = getattr(self.training_config, "create_dataset", OmegaConf.create({})); default_builder_kwargs = dict(create_dataset_config)`; :260-271 forwards `builder_kwargs` (a copy of the same dict, unfiltered) to is_source_prepared/prepare_source/is_built/build. egs3/TEMPLATE/asr/conf/training.yaml:51-53 `create_dataset: {func: src.creating_dataset.create_dataset, dataset_dir: ${dataset_dir}}`. egs3/mini_an4/asr/dataset/builder.py:64,92,136,163 all declare `**_kwargs` catch-alls. `grep -rn "create_dataset.*\.func\|\.get(\"func\"" espnet3/ egs3/` (this session) returned no matches anywhere the `func` value is actually read.
findings.suggested_fix: Either wire `create_dataset.func` up as an actual overridable factory (resolve and call it if present, falling back to the fixed builder-method protocol otherwise) or drop it from the TEMPLATE config/docs so it doesn't imply behavior the framework doesn't implement.

findings.summary: resolve_stages() silently returns an empty stage list (a complete, unannounced no-op run) for any requested name not present in the known stages list, rather than raising or warning -- reachable by any caller that bypasses argparse's own `choices=` constraint.
findings.scenario: `resolve_stages(requested, stages)` (stages_utils.py:56-69) computes `[s for s in stages if s in set(requested)]`; if none of `requested` match any name in `stages`, the result is `[]` and run_stages() then iterates zero times, doing nothing, with no error and no warning logged. For the shipped TEMPLATE/mini_an4/librispeech CLIs this is not reachable through normal use, because build_parser() constrains `--stages` with `choices=list(stages) + ["all"]` (egs3/TEMPLATE/asr/run.py:44-50), so argparse itself rejects an unrecognized stage name before resolve_stages ever sees it. The gap is real for any other caller of resolve_stages()/parse_cli_and_stage_args() directly (e.g. a test, a custom recipe runner that builds its own argparse.ArgumentParser without a matching `choices=`, or programmatic use), where a typo'd or stale stage name silently produces a run that does nothing instead of failing loudly.
findings.evidence: stages_utils.py:56-69: `if "all" in requested: return list(stages)` / `requested_set = set(requested)` / `return [s for s in stages if s in requested_set]` -- no branch for 'no overlap'. egs3/TEMPLATE/asr/run.py:44-50 `parser.add_argument("--stages", choices=list(stages) + ["all"], ...)` is what actually prevents this for the documented CLI entrypoints.
findings.suggested_fix: Raise a ValueError (listing the unrecognized names) when resolve_stages() would otherwise return an empty list from a non-empty `requested`, so misuse outside the argparse-guarded CLI path fails loudly instead of silently doing nothing.

findings.summary: run_stages() has no rank guard for any stage except the train stage's log-file naming; in multi-GPU DDP runs launched via Lightning's local subprocess launcher (not torchrun/srun), every stage other than the Lightning-managed train loop -- including create_dataset, infer, measure, pack_model, upload_model, pack_demo and upload_demo -- would re-execute once per rank, including duplicate concurrent uploads to the same Hugging Face repo.
findings.scenario: Configure trainer.strategy for multi-GPU on a single node (e.g. `devices: 2+` with the default 'auto'/DDP strategy and no torchrun/srun front-end) and request the default stage list (`python run.py --training_config ...`, no explicit --stages). ESPnet3LightningTrainer.fit() (trainer.py:239-253) delegates straight to `self.trainer.fit(...)`; for the local (non-torchrun) DDP launcher, Lightning's `_SubprocessScriptLauncher` re-executes `[sys.executable] + sys.argv` as a brand-new child process for each additional local rank once `trainer.fit()` is entered -- i.e. it re-runs `run.py` with the exact same `--stages create_dataset train_tokenizer collect_stats train infer measure pack_model upload_model pack_demo upload_demo ...` argv it was originally launched with. That child process re-executes main() from scratch: it re-parses argv, reloads configs, reconstructs the System, and calls run_stages() over the full stage list again. Nothing in run_stages(), main(), or BaseSystem checks 'am I a Lightning-spawned child rank' before running the pre-train stages (create_dataset, again, concurrently with whatever the parent process's create_dataset run is doing) or -- after this rank's `trainer.fit()` returns once DDP training completes -- the post-train stages (infer, measure, pack_model, upload_model, pack_demo, upload_demo) a second (third, ...) time per additional local rank, including duplicate concurrent `upload_model`/`upload_demo` calls to the same Hugging Face repo from multiple processes.
findings.evidence: stages_utils.py:116-197 (run_stages) only inspects rank for the "train" stage's stage_log_mode/filename choice (lines 152-173); every other stage in stages_to_run runs unconditionally regardless of `_get_process_rank()`. trainer.py:239-253 `fit()` calls `self.trainer.fit(model=self.model, ...)` directly, with no rank check before or after. No occurrence of `is_global_zero`, `LOCAL_RANK` gating, or a barrier/rank check was found anywhere in system.py, stages_utils.py, training.py, or run_utils.py for stages other than train's log naming.
findings.suggested_fix: Gate every non-train stage (and ideally create_dataset/train_tokenizer/collect_stats too) behind a rank-0-only check at the run_stages or main() level -- e.g. skip straight to a no-op for stages already completed/owned by rank 0, using torch.distributed's rank (already read by _get_process_rank) -- or document explicitly that these recipes must be launched via torchrun/srun (which does not re-execute the whole script) and never via a bare multi-device `devices=N` local launch.
